### Key Insights

1. **Templating Architecture:** Most copy-mode bindings use a chezmoi template variable (`$copyTable`) to switch between `copy-mode-vi` and `copy-mode` tables based on `enableVimMode`.

2. **Mouse Behavior:** 
   - Right-click pane menus are persistent (`-O` flag) and context-aware
   - Mouse drag end (`MouseDragEnd1Pane`) triggers copy without exiting copy-mode
   - Double-click selects a word

3. **Clipboard:** All copy operations use `tmux load-buffer -w -`, which forwards to OSC 52 automatically when `set-clipboard on` is enabled.

4. **Pane Navigation in Copy-Mode:** Only Ctrl+h/j/k/l work; these are hardcoded to `copy-mode-vi` and won't exist if `enableVimMode=false`.

150	# (jump to output start, not prompt start) is tmux 3.5+.
151	#
152	#   {  / }    previous/next prompt (the prompt line itself)
153	#   M-[ / M-] previous/next command output (line AFTER the prompt — usually
154	#             what you want for "skip to the output of the previous command")
155	# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
156	bind -T {{ $copyTable }} '{' send-keys -X previous-prompt
157	bind -T {{ $copyTable }} '}' send-keys -X next-prompt
158	bind -T {{ $copyTable }} M-[ send-keys -X previous-prompt -o
159	bind -T {{ $copyTable }} M-] send-keys -X next-prompt -o
160	
161	# =============================================================================
162	# Capture Pane Helpers
163	# =============================================================================
164	
165	# prefix + y: copy visible pane content to system clipboard
166	# `load-buffer -w -` loads into tmux's paste buffer AND forwards to the outer
167	# terminal via OSC 52 (requires `set-clipboard on` in common.conf). This works
168	# over SSH without shelling out to pbcopy/xclip on the remote host.
169	bind y run-shell "tmux capture-pane -p | tmux load-buffer -w - && tmux display-message 'Pane content copied to clipboard'"
170	
171	# prefix + Y: copy full scrollback to system clipboard
172	bind Y run-shell "tmux capture-pane -pS - | tmux load-buffer -w - && tmux display-message 'Full scrollback copied to clipboard'"
173	
174	# prefix + C-y: capture pane into fzf for line-by-line selection, yank chosen lines
175	bind C-y run-shell "\
176	  tmux capture-pane -pS - | fzf-tmux -p 80%,70% --multi --tac --no-sort \
177	    --header 'Select lines to copy (Tab=multi, Enter=copy)' \
178	    | tmux load-buffer -w - && tmux display-message 'Selected lines copied'"
179	
180	# prefix + M-y: copy the LAST command's OUTPUT to clipboard (Warp-style).
181	# Requires OSC 133 markers — if the shell doesn't emit them (non-zsh shell,
182	# DISABLE_OSC133=1, or a remote bash without our hook), selection ends up
183	# empty. Chain: enter copy-mode, jump to start of previous command's output,
184	# begin selection, jump forward to the next prompt (end of output), copy,
185	# flash confirmation.
186	bind M-y copy-mode \; \
187	  send-keys -X previous-prompt -o \; \
188	  send-keys -X begin-selection \; \
189	  send-keys -X next-prompt \; \
190	  send-keys -X copy-pipe-and-cancel "tmux load-buffer -w -" \; \
191	  display-message "Last command output copied to clipboard"
192	
193	# prefix + M-i: copy the LAST command's INPUT LINE (prompt + typed command).
194	# Same dependency on OSC 133 markers. Because we don't emit the B marker
195	# (end-of-prompt), the copied text includes prompt chrome (e.g. "❯ echo hi"
196	# not just "echo hi"). Trim in the paste target if needed. Chain: enter
197	# copy-mode, jump to the previous prompt's A marker, begin selection, jump
198	# forward to the C marker (= start of output = end of input line), copy.
199	bind M-i copy-mode \; \
200	  send-keys -X previous-prompt \; \
201	  send-keys -X begin-selection \; \
202	  send-keys -X next-prompt -o \; \
203	  send-keys -X copy-pipe-and-cancel "tmux load-buffer -w -" \; \
204	  display-message "Last command input (prompt+line) copied to clipboard"
205	
206	# =============================================================================
207	# Vim-Style Pane Navigation
208	# =============================================================================
209	
210	bind h select-pane -L
211	bind j select-pane -D
212	bind k select-pane -U
213	bind l select-pane -R
214	
215	# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
216	# vim-tmux-navigator: prefix-less Ctrl+h/j/k/l crosses tmux panes <-> vim splits
217	# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
218	# Detect if the current pane is running vim/neovim; if so forward the key,
219	# otherwise move between tmux panes. Matches christoomey/vim-tmux-navigator.
220	# Gated on chezmoi `enableVimMode` (default true). When off, Ctrl+h/j/k/l
221	# pass through to the inner shell (Ctrl+L = clear, Ctrl+H = backspace, etc.).
222	# See docs/this_repo/vim-mode.md.
223	{{ if .enableVimMode -}}
224	is_vim="ps -o state= -o comm= -t '#{pane_tty}' | grep -iqE '^[^TXZ ]+ +(\\S+\\/)?g?\\.?(view|n?vim?x?)(-wrapped)?(diff)?$'"
225	bind-key -n 'C-h' if-shell "$is_vim" 'send-keys C-h'  'select-pane -L'
226	bind-key -n 'C-j' if-shell "$is_vim" 'send-keys C-j'  'select-pane -D'
227	bind-key -n 'C-k' if-shell "$is_vim" 'send-keys C-k'  'select-pane -U'
228	bind-key -n 'C-l' if-shell "$is_vim" 'send-keys C-l'  'select-pane -R'
229	# NOTE: C-\ (select-pane -l) removed — tmux 3.4+ cannot parse C-\ in config files.
230	# Use directional C-h/j/k/l instead, or prefix+; for last-pane.
231	
232	bind-key -T copy-mode-vi 'C-h' select-pane -L
233	bind-key -T copy-mode-vi 'C-j' select-pane -D
234	bind-key -T copy-mode-vi 'C-k' select-pane -U
235	bind-key -T copy-mode-vi 'C-l' select-pane -R
236	{{- else -}}
237	# enableVimMode = false: vim-tmux-navigator omitted. Use prefix + h/j/k/l
238	# (kept below) or prefix + Arrow for pane navigation.
239	{{- end }}
240	
241	# Intuitive split bindings (| = left/right, - = top/bottom)
242	bind | split-window -h -c "#{pane_current_path}"
243	bind - split-window -v -c "#{pane_current_path}"
244	
245	# Also override default % and " so they inherit current pane's cwd (consistent with | / - and `c`)
246	bind % split-window -h -c "#{pane_current_path}"
247	bind '"' split-window -v -c "#{pane_current_path}"
248	
249	# Resize panes with prefix + H/J/K/L (5 cells)
250	bind -r H resize-pane -L 5
251	bind -r J resize-pane -D 5
252	bind -r K resize-pane -U 5
253	bind -r L resize-pane -R 5
254	
255	# Fine resize with Meta + h/j/k/l (1 cell, repeatable)
256	bind -r M-h resize-pane -L 1
257	bind -r M-j resize-pane -D 1
258	bind -r M-k resize-pane -U 1
259	bind -r M-l resize-pane -R 1
260	
261	# Quick ratio: set current pane to 75% width
262	bind + resize-pane -x 75%
263	
264	# =============================================================================
265	# Quick Window Switching (Ctrl+Number, requires CSI-u / extended-keys)
266	# =============================================================================
267	# Supplement to prefix + 1..9 (tmux built-in defaults, always available).
268	# These require extended-keys (CSI-u) support from the terminal emulator
269	# (Ghostty/cmux, Alacritty, Kitty, WezTerm). Legacy terminals (Terminal.app,
270	# plain SSH) will not send these sequences — use prefix + number instead.
271	# Note: prefix + 9 / prefix + 0 are rebound below (scode / sesh-root for
272	# current dir), so Ctrl+9 below is the only way to reach window 9 from
273	# the keyboard. Ctrl+0 mirrors prefix+0 (lightweight sesh-root) since
274	# base-index is 1 and window 0 doesn't exist.
275	
276	bind-key -n C-1 select-window -t :=1
277	bind-key -n C-2 select-window -t :=2
278	bind-key -n C-3 select-window -t :=3
279	bind-key -n C-4 select-window -t :=4
280	bind-key -n C-5 select-window -t :=5
281	bind-key -n C-6 select-window -t :=6
282	bind-key -n C-7 select-window -t :=7
283	bind-key -n C-8 select-window -t :=8
284	bind-key -n C-9 select-window -t :=9
285	bind-key -n C-0 run-shell -b "~/.config/tmux/sesh-root-here.sh '#{pane_current_path}'"
286	
287	# New window/pane inherits current path
288	bind c new-window -c "#{pane_current_path}"
289	
290	# Reload config with prefix + R
291	bind R source-file "$HOME/.tmux.conf" \; display-message "Sourced ~/.tmux.conf"
292	
293	# Session management
294	bind N command-prompt -p "New session:" "new-session -s '%%'"
295	bind X confirm-before -p "Kill session #S? (y/n)" kill-session
296	# Kill current session AND detach client (return to parent shell).
297	# Differs from `prefix + X` above, which keeps you inside tmux by
298	# switching to another session (detach-on-destroy off, common.conf).
299	# Chained via helper script because `confirm-before` takes a single
300	# tmux command; inline `\;` inside its string arg is not parsed as a
301	# command separator.
302	bind M-x confirm-before -p "Kill session #S and exit tmux? (y/n)" \
303	  "run-shell '$HOME/.config/tmux/kill-session-exit.sh'"
304	bind x confirm-before -p "Kill pane? (y/n)" kill-pane
305	bind W confirm-before -p "Kill window #W? (y/n)" kill-window
306	
307	# Manual renumber (renumber-windows on usually handles this, but kill-pane on
308	# multi-pane windows or shell-driven exits can leave gaps).
309	bind r move-window -r \; display-message "Windows renumbered"
310	
311	# =============================================================================
312	# Move/Break Windows Across Sessions (GUI tab tear-out feel)
313	# =============================================================================
314	# prefix + M : move current window to another session (interactive prompt).
315	#              Target form: "session:" (auto-pick index) or "session:index"
316	#              (use -k via "!session:index" trick? simpler: bare prompt).
317	#              Tab-completes existing sessions.
318	# prefix + B : break current pane into a new window AND move it to a target
319	#              session in one go (acts like dragging a tab out).
320	# prefix + A : link current window into another session (window appears in
321	#              both sessions; edit either, both update). Use prefix + & to
322	#              kill, or unlink-window to detach without killing.
323	#
324	# Cross-window pane operations (no top-level prefix binding — letter slots are
325	# saturated by resize-pane H/J/K/L and sesh-last S; pane join/send live in the
326	# right-click pane menu and the popup menu's Session submenu instead):
327	#   - Mark current pane:  prefix + m  (built-in)
328	#   - Pull marked pane:   right-click pane menu → "Join marked pane here"
329	#   - Push current pane:  right-click pane menu → "Send pane to..."
330	#   - Break out to new window: right-click pane menu → "Break to new window"
331	#                              or prefix + ! (built-in, same session)
332	#                              or prefix + B (break + move to chosen session)
333	
334	bind M run-shell "tmux set-environment -g _src_window '#{window_id}'" \; \
335	  display-message "Pick destination session to MOVE window into…" \; \
336	  choose-tree -Zs -F "#{session_name}" \
337	  "run-shell '~/.config/tmux/cross-session.sh move %%'"
338	bind B run-shell "tmux set-environment -g _src_pane '#{pane_id}'" \; \
339	  display-message "Pick destination session to BREAK pane into (as new window)…" \; \
340	  choose-tree -Zs -F "#{session_name}" \
341	  "run-shell '~/.config/tmux/cross-session.sh break %%'"
342	bind A run-shell "tmux set-environment -g _src_window '#{window_id}'" \; \
343	  display-message "Pick destination session to LINK window into (window lives in both)…" \; \
344	  choose-tree -Zs -F "#{session_name}" \
345	  "run-shell '~/.config/tmux/cross-session.sh link %%'"
346	
347	# prefix + E : explode — break EVERY pane in current window into its own window
348	#              within the SAME session. Use case: switching from wide screen
349	#              (multi-pane layout) to mobile/SSH where one pane per window is
350	#              easier than zooming with prefix + z. Source window keeps the
351	#              first pane; other panes become sibling windows inserted right
352	#              after it, named after each pane's current command.
353	bind E run-shell "~/.config/tmux/break-all-panes.sh"
354	
355	# =============================================================================
356	# Theme Switching (Catppuccin <-> tmux2k)
357	# =============================================================================
358	# Note: first-time switch requires `prefix + I` to install the target plugin.
359	
360	bind M-c run-shell "tmux set -g @theme_variant catppuccin; \
361	  tmux source-file ~/.tmux.conf; \
362	  tmux display-message 'Theme: catppuccin'"
363	
364	bind M-t run-shell "tmux set -g @theme_variant tmux2k; \
365	  tmux source-file ~/.tmux.conf; \
366	  tmux display-message 'Theme: tmux2k'"
367	
368	# =============================================================================
369	# Sesh (tmux session manager)
370	# =============================================================================
371	
372	# prefix + g: sesh picker in a tmux popup with fzf
373	bind-key "g" run-shell "sesh connect \"$(\
374	  sesh list --icons | fzf-tmux -p 80%,70% \
375	    --no-sort --ansi --border-label ' sesh ' --prompt '⚡  ' \
376	    --header '  ^a all ^t tmux ^g configs ^x zoxide ^d tmux kill ^f find' \
377	    --bind 'tab:down,btab:up' \
378	    --bind 'ctrl-a:change-prompt(⚡  )+reload(sesh list --icons)' \
379	    --bind 'ctrl-t:change-prompt(🪟  )+reload(sesh list -t --icons)' \
380	    --bind 'ctrl-g:change-prompt(⚙️  )+reload(sesh list -c --icons)' \
381	    --bind 'ctrl-x:change-prompt(📁  )+reload(sesh list -z --icons)' \
382	    --bind 'ctrl-f:change-prompt(🔎  )+reload(fd -H -d 2 -t d -E .Trash . ~)' \
383	    --bind 'ctrl-d:execute(tmux kill-session -t {2..})+change-prompt(⚡  )+reload(sesh list --icons)' \
384	    --preview-window 'right:55%' \
385	    --preview 'sesh preview {}' \
386	)\""
387	
388	bind -N "last-session (via sesh)" S run-shell "sesh last 2>/dev/null || tmux display-message 'No previous sesh session'"
389	
390	# prefix + 9: open repo-aware coding-agent layout (`scode`) for the current
391	# pane's directory. scode walks up from cwd to find .git; if not in a repo,
392	# the error surfaces in the tmux status line.
393	# Replaces the previous `sesh connect --root $(pwd)` binding (which had a
394	# subtle bug — $(pwd) was expanded once at config parse time, not per-press).
395	# Logic is in scode-here.sh because tmux run-shell is /bin/sh (can't see
396	# zsh functions) and the session-name + switch-client dance is non-trivial.
397	bind -N "scode for current dir (repo-aware coding layout)" 9 \
398	  run-shell -b "~/.config/tmux/scode-here.sh '#{pane_current_path}'"
399	
400	# prefix + 0: lightweight counterpart to prefix+9. Plain sesh session at
401	# the git root of the current pane's directory (no nvim/agent layout).
402	# Replaces tmux's built-in `select-window -t :=0` which always errored
403	# because base-index is 1 (no window 0 exists). Logic in sesh-root-here.sh
404	# — see that file for the two bugs in the original `sesh connect --root
405	# $(pwd)` binding (parse-time $(pwd) + misuse of --root flag).
406	bind -N "sesh-root for current dir (lightweight)" 0 \
407	  run-shell -b "~/.config/tmux/sesh-root-here.sh '#{pane_current_path}'"
408	
409	# prefix + T: sesh picker via television (tv) in a tmux popup
410	bind-key "T" display-popup -E -w 80% -h 70% -d '#{pane_current_path}' -T ' Sesh (tv) ' "tv sesh"
411	
412	# prefix + O: sesh built-in picker in a tmux popup
413	bind-key "O" display-popup -h 90% -w 50% -E "sesh picker -i"
414	
415	# prefix + U: CLI tools picker via television (tv tools)
416	bind-key "U" display-popup -E -w 80% -h 70% -d '#{pane_current_path}' -T ' CLI Tools (tv) ' "tv tools"
417	
418	# prefix + a: live coding-agent panes picker (tv agent-panes)
419	# Shows claude / cursor-agent / codex / opencode sessions currently running in
420	# any tmux pane. Enter switches focus to that pane. See:
421	#   docs/tools/agent-panes-discovery.md
422	bind-key "a" display-popup -E -w 80% -h 70% -d '#{pane_current_path}' -T ' Live agent panes (tv) ' "tv agent-panes"
423	
424	# (prefix + W is now bound earlier in this file as `kill-window`. The previous
425	# `sesh window` binding was removed because `sesh` has no `window` subcommand;
426	# pressing it printed sesh's help to a popup. See git history.)
427	
428	# =============================================================================
429	# Popup tools (display-popup -E -d '#{pane_current_path}')
430	# =============================================================================
431	# Floating scratch pane (tmux-floax) is on prefix + F (toggleable, persistent
432	# session named `float`). The bindings below are one-shot popups that close
433	# when the inner command exits — handy for "do one thing without disrupting
434	# the layout" workflows.
435	
436	# prefix + G: lazygit popup at current pane path
437	bind-key "G" display-popup -E -w 90% -h 90% -d '#{pane_current_path}' -T ' lazygit ' "lazygit"
438	
439	# prefix + ` (backtick): one-shot popup shell at current pane path.
440	# Closes when the inner shell exits (`exit` or Ctrl-D). Each invocation gets
441	# a fresh shell — no state preserved. For a persistent scratchpad with
442	# history, use floax (prefix + F) instead.
443	bind-key '`' display-popup -E -w 80% -h 80% -d '#{pane_current_path}' -T ' shell '
444	
445	# =============================================================================
446	# Help / cheatsheet
447	# =============================================================================
448	# tmux's built-in `prefix + ?` (list-keys -N) is hard to scan and can't search
449	# user-defined bindings well. We replace it with tmux-fzf's keybinding picker
450	# (fzf popup, fuzzy-searchable). The original list-keys is still reachable on
451	# `prefix + C-?` as a fallback.
452	#
453	# `prefix + /` (built-in: prompt for a key, show what it's bound to) is left
454	# alone — it's already useful for "what does THIS key do?" lookups.
455	#
456	# `?` inside the prefix + Enter popup menu opens a glow-rendered
457	# cheatsheet (curated, grouped, prettier than list-keys).
458	
459	unbind-key '?'
460	bind-key '?' run-shell -b "~/.tmux/plugins/tmux-fzf/main.sh"
461	bind-key 'C-?' list-keys -N
462	
463	# `/` inside the Enter-popup uses this; standalone prefix + / stays built-in
464	# (key-prompt). We expose the cheatsheet through the popup menu's `?` entry.
465	bind-key M-/ display-popup -E -w 80% -h 80% -T ' tmux cheatsheet ' \
466	  "glow -p ~/.config/tmux/cheatsheet.md 2>/dev/null \
467	    || less ~/.config/tmux/cheatsheet.md"
468	
469	# =============================================================================
470	# Popup Menu (prefix + Space)
471	# =============================================================================
472	# Two entry keys, same menu. The menu itself is generated by a script
473	# (`~/.config/tmux/menu.sh`) which:
474	#
475	#   1. Reads `#{client_height}` and emits a tier-trimmed row list. tmux's
476	#      `display-menu` does NOT paginate — if the menu is taller than the
477	#      terminal, the entire popup is silently suppressed (no error). The
478	#      script keeps the menu fitting on tiny mobile-SSH heights too.
479	#   2. Submenus are sibling scripts (menu-layouts.sh, menu-session.sh,
480	#      menu-sesh.sh, menu-popups.sh, menu-theme.sh, menu-system.sh). Each
481	#      `exec tmux display-menu …` so quoting context resets per submenu —
482	#      no nested-quote escaping disasters in keybindings.conf.
483	#
484	# History: an earlier flat ~50-row menu silently failed on smaller heights
485	# and was misdiagnosed as a csi-u key encoding bug, then as a quoting bug.
486	# Both real (the `\;` accelerator was broken, sesh fzf binds had nested-
487	# quote issues), but the dominant symptom — "menu doesn't open at all" —
488	# was actually menu-too-tall. See pitfalls/tmux-display-menu-silent-parse-failure.md.
489	#
490	# Discovery fallbacks if you forget the keys: `prefix + ?` (tmux-fzf fuzzy
491	# picker over every binding), `prefix + M-/` (glow cheatsheet popup), or
492	# right-click on a pane / status line.
493	
494	unbind-key Space
495	unbind-key Enter
496	bind-key Space run-shell "~/.config/tmux/menu.sh"
497	# Note: `prefix + e` was previously a popup-menu alias (added as workaround
498	# for a misdiagnosed display-menu bug — see pitfalls/tmux-display-menu-silent-fail.md).
499	# Removed so `e` is free as a sub-menu mnemonic (e.g. "Even layout: horizontal"
500	# in the window right-click menu).
501	
502	# =============================================================================
503	# Right-click menus on the keyboard (prefix + M-p / M-w / M-s)
504	# =============================================================================
505	# Keyboard equivalents of the three MouseDown3* right-click menus defined at
506	# the top of this file:
507	#
508	#   prefix + M-p  →  menu-pane.sh         (same as right-click on a pane)
509	#   prefix + M-w  →  menu-window.sh       (same as right-click on a window tab)
510	#   prefix + M-s  →  menu-status-left.sh  (same as right-click on the session
511	#                                          name in the status-left area)
512	#
513	# WHY scripts (not inline `display-menu` like the MouseDown3* bindings):
514	# `pitfalls/tmux-submenu-flash-and-bottom-right.md` — a `display-menu` launched
515	# indirectly via `run-shell` from a MouseDown3 binding has its mouse-release
516	# event leaked into the menu, dismissing it instantly. So the MouseDown3*
517	# bodies MUST stay inline above. Keyboard activation has no pending mouse
518	# event, so a script wrapper is safe — and keeps this file shorter. The menu
519	# bodies are duplicated between the MouseDown3* bindings here and the scripts
520	# under dot_config/tmux/menu-*.sh; each location carries a "sync me" comment.
521	#
522	# Requires terminal Option-as-Meta on macOS (already set by the repo's
523	# Ghostty/cmux config: `macos-option-as-alt = left`). On Linux terminals the
524	# Alt modifier is sent natively.
525	
526	bind -N "right-click pane menu (keyboard)"      M-p run-shell "~/.config/tmux/menu-pane.sh"
527	bind -N "right-click window menu (keyboard)"    M-w run-shell "~/.config/tmux/menu-window.sh"
528	bind -N "right-click status-left menu (keyboard)" M-s run-shell "~/.config/tmux/menu-status-left.sh"
529

38	
39	# Open highlighted selection in copy-mode: o = open, C-o = open in $EDITOR, S = search
40	set -g @plugin 'tmux-plugins/tmux-open'
41	set -g @open-S 'https://www.google.com/search?q='
42	
43	# tmux-fzf: replaces the ugly built-in `prefix + ?` (list-keys dump) with an
44	# fzf popup over EVERY binding (incl. user-defined), plus session/window/pane/
45	# command/process/clipboard pickers. The plugin's launch key defaults to `F`
46	# which collides with tmux-floax — set it to `M-Z` (an unused key) so the
47	# plugin's auto-binding doesn't shadow floax. Our real entry point is
48	# `prefix + ?` (rebound in keybindings.conf).
49	# NOTE: `TMUX_FZF_LAUNCH_KEY=""` does NOT disable the auto-bind — the
50	# plugin's `[ -z "$VAR" ]` check treats empty as unset and falls back to `F`.
51	set -g @plugin 'sainnhe/tmux-fzf'
52	TMUX_FZF_LAUNCH_KEY="M-Z"
53	TMUX_FZF_OPTIONS="-p -w 80% -h 70% -m"
54	TMUX_FZF_ORDER="keybinding|session|window|pane|command|process|clipboard"
55	TMUX_FZF_PREVIEW=1
56	
57	# =============================================================================
58	# General Settings
59	# =============================================================================
60	
61	# No ESC delay (critical for Neovim and coding agents)
62	set -sg escape-time 0
63	
64	# Enable mouse support
65	setw -g mouse on
66	
67	# Use vi mode keys in copy mode (gated on chezmoi `enableVimMode` —
68	# default true; false → emacs copy-mode keymap. See docs/this_repo/vim-mode.md.)
69	setw -g mode-keys {{ if .enableVimMode }}vi{{ else }}emacs{{ end }}
70	
71	# Larger scrollback buffer
72	set -g history-limit 50000
73	
74	# Don't push the pre-clear screen contents into scrollback when a TUI issues a
75	# full-screen clear (ED). Streaming coding agents (Claude Code, OpenCode, etc.)
76	# that run on the main screen (not alternate-screen) otherwise leave ghost
77	# frames in history every repaint. Alt-screen apps (vim, htop) are unaffected.
78	# Default in tmux 3.3+ is `on`; we explicitly turn it off for cleaner scrollback.
79	# See pitfalls/tmux-scrollback-tui-repaint-ghosting.md.
80	set -g scroll-on-clear off
81	
82	# 1-indexed windows and panes
83	set -g base-index 1
84	setw -g pane-base-index 1
85	set -g renumber-windows on
86	
87	# Focus events for Vim autoread compatibility
88	set -g focus-events on
89	
90	# If the current session is destroyed, switch to another one instead of detaching
91	set -g detach-on-destroy off
92	
93	# Status bar visibility (position is set per-theme)
94	set-option -g status on
95	
96	# Window activity / silence / bell flags
97	# These drive the per-window flag glyphs (`#` activity, `~` silence, `!` bell)
98	# that Catppuccin's `window-status-format` already includes via #{window_flags}.
99	# Use case: glance at the tab bar to see which non-current window produced
100	# output (`#`) or has been quiet for a while (`~`). Useful for long builds /
101	# tests / pueue queues running in background panes.
102	#
103	# Limitation for LLM agent panes: opencode/claude run a spinner while the
104	# model is thinking, so from tmux's POV the pane is *always* active —
105	# `monitor-silence` will not fire for "agent waiting on user". For true
106	# semantic state (running / idle / error) on agent panes, see
107	# backlog/tmux-window-status-indicators.md.
108	#
109	# `visual-*` are kept off so the message line never spams; the flag in the
110	# tab list is the only visible signal.
111	setw -g monitor-activity on
112	setw -g monitor-bell on
113	setw -g monitor-silence 0
114	set -g visual-activity off
115	set -g visual-silence off
116	set -g visual-bell off
117	
118	# Status-bar messages (display-message) — default 750ms is too short to read
119	# multi-word confirmations like "Moved to foo:3 (zsh)" before they vanish.
120	# 0 = stay until the next key event (the key still does its normal action;
121	# only the message gets cleared). Trade-off: occasionally a stale message
122	# lingers if you stop typing, but no important confirmation is ever missed.
123	set -g display-time 0
124	
125	# =============================================================================
126	# Terminal & Key Compatibility
127	# =============================================================================
128	
129	set -s default-terminal 'tmux-256color'
130	set -as terminal-features ",xterm-256color:RGB"
131	
132	# Forward extended keys (CSI-u) so Ctrl+/, Shift+Enter etc. reach TUIs.
133	#
134	# Use `on` (NOT `always`):
135	#   - `on`: emit CSI-u only when a key has NO legacy encoding (Shift+Enter,
136	#     Ctrl+Enter, Ctrl+/, Ctrl+digit). Keys with legacy encoding (Ctrl+letter
137	#     including Ctrl+J = LF, Ctrl+M = CR, Ctrl+I = TAB) keep their classic
138	#     bytes.
139	#   - `always`: emit CSI-u for EVERY modifier+key combo, including ones with
140	#     a legacy encoding. This breaks ble.sh paste handling because each `\n`
141	#     in pasted content gets re-encoded as `ESC[106;5u` (Ctrl+J as CSI-u),
142	#     and ble.sh inserts the escape sequence as literal text instead of as
143	#     a newline. See pitfalls/tmux-extended-keys-always-paste.md.
144	#
145	# Net result on `on`: TUIs that need Ctrl+Enter / Shift+Enter (Claude Code,
146	# Neovim, etc.) still get them; paste of multi-line text into ble.sh works
147	# correctly; legacy `Ctrl+letter` shortcuts in shells / tmux / TUIs keep
148	# their normal encodings.
149	set -s extended-keys on
150	if-shell 'tmux -V | grep -qE "tmux ([3-9]\.[5-9]|[3-9]\.[1-9][0-9]|[4-9]\.)"' \
151	  'set -s extended-keys-format csi-u'
152	set -as terminal-features 'xterm*:extkeys'
153	
154	# OSC 52 clipboard (works over SSH)
155	set -g set-clipboard on
156	
157	# Declare OSC 52 support explicitly for common outer terminals. tmux 3.2+ only
158	# emits OSC 52 when it believes the outer terminal supports it; most modern
159	# terminals (Ghostty, Alacritty, iTerm2, kitty, WezTerm) do. Without these
160	# hints tmux falls back to terminfo's `Ms` capability, which is absent from
161	# the `tmux-256color` entry shipped by many distros, so yanks from inner
162	# apps (e.g. Neovim over SSH) silently drop.
163	set -as terminal-features ",xterm*:clipboard"
164	set -as terminal-features ",ghostty*:clipboard"
165	set -as terminal-features ",alacritty*:clipboard"
166	
167	# Allow OSC passthrough (for terminal images, sixel, etc.)
168	set -g allow-passthrough on
169
```
</details></tool-use>

6	
7	# Auto-clone on first use (TPM only installs on prefix + I)
8	if-shell '[ ! -d ~/.tmux/plugins/tmux ]' \
9	  'run-shell "git clone --depth 1 https://github.com/catppuccin/tmux.git ~/.tmux/plugins/tmux 2>/dev/null"'
10

12	set -g status-position top
13	set -g status-justify left
14	
15	# Catppuccin options -- must be set BEFORE running the plugin
16	set -g @catppuccin_flavor 'mocha'
17	set -g @catppuccin_window_status_style 'rounded'
18	
19	# Window text (what each tab shows). #I = index, #W = window name.
20	#
21	# Two parallel per-window user-options stack into the tab label:
22	#
23	#   #{?@workmux_status, #{@workmux_status},}
24	#     workmux agent state (🤖 working / 💬 waiting / ✅ done), written by
25	#     `workmux set-window-status` from Claude Code hooks
26	#     (dot_claude/modify_settings.json) and the OpenCode plugin
27	#     (dot_config/opencode/plugins/workmux-status.ts). `waiting` and `done`
28	#     auto-clear on window focus; `working` is sticky and relies on `Stop` /
29	#     `session.idle` hooks to transition to `done`. Cleared from CLI via
30	#     `wmclear` (dot_config/shell/38_workmux.sh) or from the right-click tab
31	#     menu's "Clear agent status" entry (dot_config/tmux/keybindings.conf.tmpl).
32	#     We set `status_format: false` in dot_config/workmux/config.yaml so workmux
33	#     does NOT also append its own format per-tmux-session — that path is
34	#     per-session and doesn't survive new sessions or chezmoi diffs.
35	#
36	#   #{?@bookmark_status, #{@bookmark_status},}
37	#     Manual user tag (⭐/📌/🔖/🚩), toggled from the right-click tab menu via
38	#     ~/.config/tmux/toggle-bookmark.sh. Independent of workmux — both render
39	#     side-by-side so a window can show e.g. `1: shell 🤖 ⭐` (agent working +
40	#     bookmarked). Settable from CLI too: `tmux_status_set bookmark <glyph>`
41	#     (dot_config/shell/60_tmux_status.sh).
42	#
43	# See docs/tools/workmux.md for the full integration story.
44	set -g @catppuccin_window_text ' #W#{?@workmux_status, #{@workmux_status},}#{?@bookmark_status, #{@bookmark_status},}'
45	set -g @catppuccin_window_current_text ' #W#{?window_zoomed_flag, 󰊓 ,}#{?@workmux_status, #{@workmux_status},}#{?@bookmark_status, #{@bookmark_status},}'
46	set -g @catppuccin_window_number_position 'left'
47	
48	# Module tweaks
49	set -g @catppuccin_directory_text "#{b:pane_current_path}"
50	set -g @catppuccin_date_time_text "%Y-%m-%d %H:%M"
51	
52	# Load plugin -- this populates @catppuccin_status_*, window-status-format,
53	# window-status-current-format with Catppuccin styling
54	run '~/.tmux/plugins/tmux/catppuccin.tmux'
55	
56	# Responsive status line: status-left/status-right are conditional formats
57	# that select module bundles based on each client's #{client_width}, so
58	# multi-client attaches at different widths each see the right tier without
59	# stomping on each other.
60	run '~/.config/tmux/responsive.sh'
61	
62	# NOTE: intentionally do NOT override window-status-format /
63	# window-status-current-format here -- the plugin has already set those based
64	# on @catppuccin_window_status_style above, and overriding them with
65	# non-existent v1 variables wipes the window list.

## Tmux Configuration Report: Mouse Selection & Copy-Mode-VI Behavior

### 1. **Mode-Keys Setting (VI vs Emacs)**
**File:** `/Volumes/Data/caches/local-share-data/chezmoi/dot_config/tmux/common.conf.tmpl`  
**Line 69:** `setw -g mode-keys {{ if .enableVimMode }}vi{{ else }}emacs{{ end }}`

This is **templated on the chezmoi `enableVimMode` prompt** (default `true`). When enabled, copy-mode uses vi keybindings; when disabled, it switches to emacs mode.

---

### 2. **Copy-Mode-VI Key Table Bindings (Lines 137–142)**
**File:** `/Volumes/Data/caches/local-share-data/chezmoi/dot_config/tmux/keybindings.conf.tmpl`

The configuration uses a **template variable** `$copyTable` (line 9–10) that dynamically selects `copy-mode-vi` (when `enableVimMode=true`) or `copy-mode` (when disabled). Here are the bindings:

| Line | Binding | Action | Note |
|------|---------|--------|------|
| 137 | `bind -T {{ $copyTable }} v send-keys -X begin-selection` | Start selection with `v` | Works in both copy-mode and copy-mode-vi |
| 138 | `bind -T {{ $copyTable }} V send-keys -X select-line` | Line selection with `V` | Vim-style block selection |
| 139 | `bind -T {{ $copyTable }} C-v send-keys -X rectangle-toggle` | Rectangle/block select with `Ctrl-v` | Vim-style rectangular selection |
| 140 | `bind -T {{ $copyTable }} y send-keys -X copy-selection-and-cancel` | Yank and exit with `y` | Exits copy-mode after yanking |
| 141 | `bind -T {{ $copyTable }} MouseDragEnd1Pane send-keys -X copy-selection` | **Mouse drag to copy** | Copy on mouse release, stays in copy-mode |
| 142 | `bind -T {{ $copyTable }} DoubleClick1Pane select-pane \; send-keys -X select-word` | **Double-click word selection** | Select pane first, then select word |

**Key distinction:** `MouseDragEnd1Pane` (line 141) uses `copy-selection` (stays in copy-mode), while the `y` binding (line 140) uses `copy-selection-and-cancel` (exits).

### 3. **Copy-Mode-VI Navigation (Lines 156–159)**
**File:** `/Volumes/Data/caches/local-share-data/chezmoi/dot_config/tmux/keybindings.conf.tmpl`

Command-boundary navigation (Warp-style, requires OSC 133 shell markers):

| 157 | `bind -T {{ $copyTable }} '}' send-keys -X next-prompt` | Jump to next prompt line |
| 158 | `bind -T {{ $copyTable }} M-[ send-keys -X previous-prompt -o` | Jump to previous command output start |
| 159 | `bind -T {{ $copyTable }} M-] send-keys -X next-prompt -o` | Jump to next command output start |

**Line 26:** The conditional logic: `if-shell -F -t = "#{||:#{mouse_any_flag},#{&&:#{pane_in_mode},#{?#{m/r:(copy|view)-mode,#{pane_mode}},0,1}}}"`

### 7. **Clipboard Integration (OSC 52)**

**Copy helpers using clipboard (Lines 169–204):**

| Line | Binding | Command | Mechanism |
|------|---------|---------|-----------|
| 169 | `prefix + y` | `tmux capture-pane -p \| tmux load-buffer -w -` | Copy visible pane to clipboard via OSC 52 |

| 186–191 | `prefix + M-y` | Chain: enter copy-mode → jump to previous command output → begin selection → copy to clipboard | **Warp-style:** copy last command output |
| 199–204 | `prefix + M-i` | Chain: enter copy-mode → jump to previous prompt → begin selection → copy | **Warp-style:** copy last command input (prompt + line) |

All use `tmux load-buffer -w -` which pipes output to both the tmux paste buffer AND the outer terminal via OSC 52.

**File:** `/Volumes/Data/caches/local-share-data/chezmoi/dot_config/tmux/keybindings.conf.tmpl`

When `enableVimMode` is set:

1. **Line 10:** `copy-mode-vi` table is selected for main copy bindings

3. **Lines 232–235:** Copy-mode-vi pane navigation (Ctrl+hjkl) is included

When `enableVimMode=false`:

- Vim-tmux-navigator is completely omitted
- Pane navigation in copy-mode uses prefix + h/j/k/l or arrow keys

| Double-click select-word | keybindings.conf.tmpl:142 | Templated ($copyTable) | `DoubleClick1Pane` → select-word |
| Prompt navigation ({/}/M-[/M-]) | keybindings.conf.tmpl:156–159 | Templated ($copyTable) | OSC 133 dependent |
| Pane nav in copy-mode (Ctrl+hjkl) | keybindings.conf.tmpl:232–235 | **Hardcoded copy-mode-vi only** | Not templated |
| Vim-tmux-navigator | keybindings.conf.tmpl:223–228 | Templated (enableVimMode) | Conditional block |
| Mouse right-click menus | keybindings.conf.tmpl:19–125 | Static | 3 menus with -O (persistent) |
| OSC 52 clipboard | common.conf.tmpl:155, 163–165 | Static | Always on |
| Clipboard helpers (y/Y/C-y/M-y/M-i) | keybindings.conf.tmpl:169–204 | Static | Uses load-buffer -w |
| Mouse enabled | common.conf.tmpl:65 | Static | `mouse on` |

---

### Key Insights

1. **Templating Architecture:** Most copy-mode bindings use a chezmoi template variable (`$copyTable`) to switch between `copy-mode-vi` and `copy-mode` tables based on `enableVimMode`.

2. **Mouse Behavior:** 
   - Right-click pane menus are persistent (`-O` flag) and context-aware
   - Mouse drag end (`MouseDragEnd1Pane`) triggers copy without exiting copy-mode
   - Double-click selects a word

3. **Clipboard:** All copy operations use `tmux load-buffer -w -`, which forwards to OSC 52 automatically when `set-clipboard on` is enabled.

4. **Pane Navigation in Copy-Mode:** Only Ctrl+h/j/k/l work; these are hardcoded to `copy-mode-vi` and won't exist if `enableVimMode=false`.

I now understand the current setup precisely. Let me explain what's happening before asking how you'd like it changed.

## What the config currently does

The relevant line is `dot_config/tmux/keybindings.conf.tmpl:141`:

```tmux
bind -T copy-mode-vi MouseDragEnd1Pane send-keys -X copy-selection
```

`copy-selection` (not `-and-cancel`) → **copies on mouse-release but stays in copy-mode**. That's exactly your "本機馬上 copy 但還在 copy mode" observation. The `y` key at line 140 is `copy-selection-and-cancel` (copy + exit).

## Why local ≠ remote (it's not this binding)

This binding only governs **tmux's own (outer) copy-mode**, which only engages when the active pane is plain local content. For a remote pane running a **mouse-aware app** (most likely a *nested tmux* on the remote, or remote vim), tmux's default `MouseDrag1Pane` sees `mouse_any_flag` set and **forwards the drag to the remote app** (`send-keys -M`) instead of entering its own copy-mode. So the "visual-select-then-`y`" you like on remote panes is actually the **remote tmux's** behavior, not this repo's. (A plain remote shell with no mouse app would behave identically to local.)

So to make your *local/outer* tmux feel the same way, we change line 141.

## On the right-click "Copy" idea — no real conflict

The pane right-click menu (`MouseDown3Pane`, line 24) only shows **when NOT in copy-mode** — line 25's conditional forwards the mouse instead whenever `pane_in_mode` is copy/view. Since you only have a selection *while in* copy-mode, the two states are mutually exclusive: a right-click-to-copy can live in the copy-mode table without ever colliding with the pane menu.

Let me confirm which behavior you want before writing the plan.

# Plan: vim-idiomatic mouse copy in tmux copy-mode

## Context

Today, dragging the mouse in a **local** tmux pane copies immediately on release but
leaves you sitting in copy-mode (`copy-selection`), while a **remote** pane appears to
"visual-select then press `y`". The user prefers the latter feel everywhere and asked
whether a right-click "Copy" could exist without clashing with the pane context menu.

Root cause of the local≠remote difference (for the record, **not** a bug to fix):
`dot_config/tmux/keybindings.conf.tmpl:141` binds `MouseDragEnd1Pane → copy-selection`,
which only governs tmux's **own (outer) copy-mode** — engaged only for plain local
content. A remote pane running a mouse-aware app (typically a *nested tmux* or vim) sets
`mouse_any_flag`, so tmux's default `MouseDrag1Pane` **forwards** the drag to the remote
app instead of entering its own copy-mode. The select-then-`y` behavior on remote panes
is therefore the *remote* tmux's config, not this repo's.

Goal: make the **local/outer** copy-mode behave the vim way — drag highlights only, and an
explicit action (key `y`, right-click, or double-click) does the copy **and exits**
copy-mode (no "stuck in copy-mode, must hit `q`" experience).

## Changes — all in `dot_config/tmux/keybindings.conf.tmpl`

`$copyTable` (line 9-10) is `copy-mode-vi` when `enableVimMode` is on, `copy-mode` otherwise.
All edits use `$copyTable` so they stay correct under both flag states.

### 1. Drag = select-only (line 141)

\```tmux
# before
bind -T {{ $copyTable }} MouseDragEnd1Pane send-keys -X copy-selection
# after
bind -T {{ $copyTable }} MouseDragEnd1Pane send-keys -X stop-selection
\```

`stop-selection` keeps the highlight active without copying, so the existing
`y` binding (line 140, `copy-selection-and-cancel`) does the copy+exit.

### 2. Double-click = select word AND copy+exit (line 142)

\```tmux
# before
bind -T {{ $copyTable }} DoubleClick1Pane select-pane \; send-keys -X select-word
# after
bind -T {{ $copyTable }} DoubleClick1Pane select-pane \; send-keys -X select-word \; send-keys -X copy-selection-and-cancel
\```

### 3. Right-click on an active selection = copy+exit (wrap the `MouseDown3Pane` binding, lines 24-50)

Wrap the existing `if-shell` in one outer `if-shell` that fires **only when a selection
is present in copy-mode**; otherwise the current logic (forward `send -M`, or show the
pane menu) is preserved byte-for-byte:

\```tmux
bind-key -n MouseDown3Pane \
  if-shell -F -t = "#{&&:#{?#{m/r:(copy|view)-mode,#{pane_mode}},1,0},#{selection_present}}" \
    { send-keys -X copy-selection-and-cancel } \
    { if-shell -F -t = "#{||:#{mouse_any_flag},#{&&:#{pane_in_mode},#{?#{m/r:(copy|view)-mode,#{pane_mode}},0,1}}}" \
        { select-pane -t = ; send-keys -M } \
        { display-menu -O -T "..." -t = -x M -y M \
            ...existing menu body unchanged... } }
\```

Why no conflict (confirmed from the code): the pane context menu only appears when **not**
in copy-mode; a selection only exists **while in** copy-mode — mutually exclusive states.
Right-click in copy-mode *without* a selection still falls through to the existing branch
(shows the menu), so that behavior is unchanged.

**Menu-body duplication rule does NOT trigger here.** `dot_config/tmux/menu-pane.sh` (the
keyboard-equivalent `prefix + M-p`) mirrors only the **menu body**, which is untouched —
we add a wrapper around it, not inside it. No edit to `menu-pane.sh`.

### "No stuck in copy-mode" guarantee

Every *copy* path uses an `-and-cancel` variant → copies and exits:
- `y` (line 140) — already `copy-selection-and-cancel`
- double-click (line 142) — adds `copy-selection-and-cancel`
- right-click on selection — `copy-selection-and-cancel`

Only the bare drag-release is `stop-selection` (highlight, no copy) by design; exit it via
`y` / right-click / `Escape` / `q`.

1. Render and parse-check the template into a throwaway tmux server:

   - re-select, **right-click** → copies + exits;
   - **double-click** a word → word copied + exits;
   - right-click with **no** selection (enter copy-mode via `prefix [`, no select) → pane
     menu still appears;
   - right-click in **normal** mode → pane menu appears (unchanged).
4. Confirm `enableVimMode=false` path still parses (bindings target `copy-mode` table).
5. `uv run mkdocs build --strict` if any `docs/**` file changed.

- `docs/tools/tmux/` — find the copy-mode / mouse section (grep for `MouseDragEnd1Pane`,
  `copy-selection`, `DoubleClick`) and update the described behavior: drag = select-only,
  `y`/right-click/double-click = copy+exit.
- `docs/shells/keybindings.md` — update if it documents tmux copy-mode mouse behavior.
- Refresh the inline help comment block at lines 131-135 if it implies drag auto-copies.
- No new alias/function, so no `docs/shells/aliases.md` row. `enableVimMode` catalog
  (`docs/this_repo/vim-mode.md`) already lists `keybindings.conf.tmpl`; no new file to add.

## Remote / SSH considerations (this config also runs on remote boxes)

This same config is deployed to remote machines, so the edits must give a good experience
when tmux is running **on the remote** and reached via an SSH terminal (directly, or as a
nested tmux under a local tmux).

- **Clipboard reaches the local machine, unchanged by this work.** The copy actions
  (`copy-selection-and-cancel`) honor `set-clipboard on` and emit **OSC 52**, which the
  repo already wires up: `common.conf.tmpl:155` (`set -g set-clipboard on`),
  `:163-165` (`terminal-features …:clipboard` for `xterm*`/`ghostty*`/`alacritty*`), and
  `allow-passthrough on` so OSC 52 propagates **up through an outer/local tmux** when this
  is the nested remote tmux. No new clipboard plumbing is needed — we reuse it.
- **`stop-selection` is internal-only** (no escape sequences) → fully transparent over SSH.
- **Mouse events** (drag / double-click / right-click) are reported by the *local* terminal
  to the remote tmux over the SSH tty; `mouse on` (`common.conf.tmpl:65`) already enables
  reporting. No change.
- **Pre-existing caveat (call out, do not fix here):** OSC 52 clipboard only works if the
  connecting terminal's `TERM` matches the `terminal-features` clipboard allowlist
  (`xterm*`/`ghostty*`/`alacritty*`). SSHing from a terminal advertising a different `TERM`
  (e.g. bare `screen`/`tmux-256color` with no clipboard feature) means the *copy still
  lands in the tmux paste buffer* (paste within tmux works) but won't reach the OS
  clipboard — same as today. Widening that allowlist is out of scope.

## Verification (Hard rule: validate config with the app, not just syntax)

1. Render and parse-check the template into a throwaway tmux server:

   chezmoi cat ~/.config/tmux/keybindings.conf > /tmp/kb.conf

   ```
   (must exit 0 with no parse error from the nested `if-shell`/`display-menu` braces).
2. `chezmoi apply` on the local box, then `tmux source-file ~/.config/tmux/tmux.conf`
   (or `tmux kill-server` + reattach).
3. Manual smoke in a local pane:
   - drag-select → text highlights, nothing copied yet, still in copy-mode;
   - press `y` → clipboard has it (verify via paste / `tmux show-buffer`), back to normal mode;
   - re-select, **right-click** → copies + exits;
   - **double-click** a word → word copied + exits;
   - right-click with **no** selection (enter copy-mode via `prefix [`, no select) → pane
     menu still appears;
   - right-click in **normal** mode → pane menu appears (unchanged).
4. Confirm `enableVimMode=false` path still parses (bindings target `copy-mode` table).
5. **SSH/remote smoke:** `chezmoi apply` on a remote box, SSH in from a clipboard-capable
   terminal (ghostty/alacritty/xterm), repeat the drag→`y` / double-click / right-click
   tests in a remote pane, and confirm the text lands in the **local** OS clipboard
   (paste outside the terminal). Repeat once nested under a local tmux to confirm OSC 52
   passthrough still reaches the local clipboard.
6. `uv run mkdocs build --strict` if any `docs/**` file changed.

175:- The **keyboard** path doesn't have that queued mouse event, so a script is safe — and keeps `keybindings.conf` short.
181:`display-menu` does not paginate. If the menu is taller than the terminal, the entire popup is **silently suppressed** (no error, nothing in `tmux show-messages`). Both the mouse and keyboard triggers are equally affected — the keyboard variant does NOT rescue the menu on small terminals. The window-tab menu is currently 23 rows so it will not appear on terminals smaller than ~26 rows. That diagnosis was wrong. The actual failure was that the inline 50-row flat menu was **taller than the terminal**, and tmux silently suppresses oversized menus per `man tmux` ("If the menu is too large to fit on the terminal, it is not displayed."). Both `Space` and `Enter` were always bindable; the keysym story was a red herring. Full debugging trail in [`pitfalls/tmux-display-menu-silent-fail.md`](../../../pitfalls/tmux-display-menu-silent-fail.md). The menu was bound to both `Space` (canonical) and `e` (alias) for a while; the `e` alias has since been **removed** to free `e` as a sub-menu mnemonic (e.g. "Even layout: horizontal" in the window right-click menu). ## What changed

All in `dot_config/tmux/keybindings.conf.tmpl` (templated on `$copyTable`, so correct under both `enableVimMode` states):

1. **Drag = select-only** — `MouseDragEnd1Pane`: `copy-selection` → `stop-selection`. Highlights without copying; `y` (already `copy-selection-and-cancel`) does the copy+exit. This is the vim-visual feel you preferred from the remote panes.
2. **Double-click = select word + copy+exit** — appended `copy-selection-and-cancel`.
3. **Right-click on a selection = copy+exit** — wrapped the existing `MouseDown3Pane` `if-shell` in an outer gate: `selection_present` in copy/view-mode → `copy-selection-and-cancel`; otherwise the original forward/menu logic runs **byte-for-byte unchanged**. No conflict with the pane menu, since a selection only exists in copy-mode and the menu only shows outside it.

Every copy path uses `-and-cancel`, so copying always exits copy-mode — your "don't get stuck needing `q`" requirement. And because the repo already has `set-clipboard on` + OSC 52 + `allow-passthrough on`, these copies reach the local clipboard even when this tmux runs on a remote box over SSH (including nested under a local tmux).

Docs updated in sync: `docs/tools/tmux/keybindings.md` + its `keybindings.zh-TW.md` mirror.
